name: Rolen Depot Steel-Toe Work Boot
description: Low-profile lace-up boot in scuffed black synth-leather with a visible steel toe cap and a thick rubber lug sole. Yellow contrast stitching around the welt is the only decorative element. Built to handle wet concrete floors and metal shavings without complaint.
functionality: Steel toe protection rated to 200J impact, oil-resistant sole, and waterproof seam sealing for wet industrial environments.
what_it_says: You don't think about your feet because these boots handle it — that's the whole point.
story_hooks: These boots are sold in bulk to three major corponations — meaning the same boot walks both sides of a labor dispute.
A pair found in a locker room has the steel toe cap removed and something else welded in — denser, heavier, custom.

physical_description.visual_profile: Chunky, utilitarian ankle boot with aggressive stance. Stubby silhouette, purposefully unglamorous. Steel toe cap protrudes visibly at the front, creating a squared-off profile. Worn appearance despite being functionally new.
physical_description.fit: Snug around the ankle, roomy in the toe box for thick socks or minor swelling. Compression-fitted heel cup, minimal arch support—designed for 12-hour shifts on concrete.
physical_description.primary_material: Scuffed black synth-leather over ballistic weave toe reinforcement. Thick rubber lug sole, heat-treated to resist thermal shock.
physical_description.texture: Matte, slightly waxy synth-leather with visible scuff marks and micro-creasing. Rubber sole has deep, defined treads. Yellow stitching sits raised against the leather.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black dominant, bright safety yellow contrast stitching along the welt seam. Steel toe cap shows light oxidation patina. Sole is industrial gray-black.
physical_description.closures: Five-eyelet lace-up with standard paracord laces, often replaced with electrical tape or zip-ties on active workers.
distinctive_features: Visible steel toe cap with slight weathering
Yellow welt stitching—practical visibility marker, not decoration
Deep rubber lugs, asymmetrical wear pattern typical after 500+ hours
Rolen Depot stamped logo on tongue tab
Oil and solvent stains common in wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Affordable workhorse, not salvage but not aspirational.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by fabrication floor workers, Iowan Behemoth handlers, maintenance crews, transit workers. Signals honest labor, early-shift clock-in, no pretense.
physical_description.condition_typical: Scuffed and creased within first week. Laces replaced monthly. Sole tread remains deep for 18+ months of daily wear. Minor seam separation possible after year two.
